texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.01.2023. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and he has spent huge amount towards medicine, nourishment, transportation and conveyance etc.,. Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as security guard and he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest. The respondent No.1 in his written statement contending that he is the RC owner of Car baring Reg. No. KL46V7327 and it has insured with second respondent. Further, denied the involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of first respondent in respect of offending Car and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further contended that, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties, as the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were not made as parties to the proceedings. Further SCCH4 5 MVC No.843/2023 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the petitioner suddenly tried to u turn as such the petitioner has attributed sole negligence for causing the accident. There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Car. The petitioner riding the motorcycle without having DL, not wearing safety helmet and thus the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, he is not entitled for any compensation. Further both the respondents denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.
